hero.title: Welcome to the CriptEnv Documentation
hero.subtitle: Everything you need to manage your secrets with military-grade security — from the CLI to the dashboard, from the API to CI/CD integrations.

whatIs.title: What is CriptEnv?
whatIs.paragraph1: CriptEnv is an open-source secrets management platform with a Zero-Knowledge architecture. An alternative to Doppler and Infisical, it lets developers and teams manage environment variables, API keys and sensitive credentials with end-to-end encryption.
whatIs.paragraph2: All secrets are encrypted 100% client-side with AES-256-GCM. The server never receives plaintext data — even with full access to the database, it is impossible to decrypt your credentials.

zeroKnowledge.title: Zero-Knowledge
zeroKnowledge.description: Secrets are encrypted 100% client-side. The server stores only ciphertext — it never sees your real data.

consistent.title: Consistent
consistent.description: CLI and API share the same semantics. What you do in the terminal you can do over HTTP and vice versa.

secureByDefault.title: Secure by default
secureByDefault.description: AES-256-GCM with PBKDF2-HKDF. No plaintext in logs, no token exposure, no data compromise.

concepts.title: Core Concepts
concepts.subtitle: Understand how projects, environments, vaults and the remote CLI connect to protect secrets end to end.
concepts.zeroKnowledgeCallout: CriptEnv is zero-knowledge: secrets are encrypted on the client and the server stores only encrypted blobs.

zeroKnowledge.title: Zero-Knowledge
zeroKnowledge.description: All encryption happens on your device. The API never receives plaintext secrets or the project's Vault password.

projects.title: Projects
projects.description: Projects group related secrets and have their own Vault password to protect your data.

environments.title: Environments
environments.description: Environments separate configuration by stage, such as development, staging and production.

remoteVault.title: Remote Vault
remoteVault.description: The remote vault is the source of truth. It stores encrypted blobs and stays in sync across CLI, web and team.

vaultPassword.title: Vault Password
vaultPassword.description: Project password used only on the client to derive keys, decrypt in memory and prove vault access.

importExport.title: Import/Export
importExport.description: Push imports .env files into the remote vault. Pull exports remote secrets to local files.

howItWorks.title: Zero-Knowledge — How does it work?
howItWorks.step1: The CLI reads the project Vault password via prompt or CRIPTENV_VAULT_PASSWORD.
howItWorks.step2: The environment key is derived locally with PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 and HKDF.
howItWorks.step3: Secrets are encrypted or decrypted in memory with AES-256-GCM.
howItWorks.step4: The API receives only ciphertext, IV, auth tag, checksum and metadata.

concepts.vaultPasswordLostTip: If the project's Vault password is lost, that project's encrypted secrets cannot be recovered by the server.

projects.title: Projects and Environments
projects.text: Projects are collaboration namespaces. Environments isolate values by stage without mixing production, staging and development.

remoteCli.title: CLI as a Remote Terminal
remoteCli.text: The CLI does not keep a local secrets vault as its main flow. It resolves project and environment through the API, downloads encrypted blobs, operates in memory and sends the new encrypted blobs back.

vercel.description: Set up automatic environment variable sync between CriptEnv and Vercel. As soon as you update your secrets in CriptEnv, they are propagated to your Vercel projects.

step1.body: Go to <link>vercel.com/account/tokens</link> and create a new token with write permission.

step2.body: In the CriptEnv dashboard, go to Project → Integrations → Vercel and paste the token. Select the Vercel project you want to sync.

render.title: Render integration
render.description: Connect CriptEnv to Render to manage your Environment Groups in one place. Keep your secrets synced automatically between CriptEnv and your Render services.

step1.title: Create a Render API key
step1.body: In Render, go to Account Settings → API Keys and create a new API key. Write the value down: it is shown only once.

step2.title: Connect Render in CriptEnv
step2.body: In the CriptEnv dashboard, go to Project → Integrations → Render. Enter the Render API key and select the Environment Group you want to sync.

step3.title: Choose the variables to sync
step3.body: Choose which CriptEnv variables are synced. You can sync every variable in an environment or pick them one by one.

step4.title: Turn on sync
step4.body: Turn on automatic sync. From then on, changes to CriptEnv secrets are reflected in Render automatically.

render.groupsTip: Render Environment Groups let you share variables across multiple services. Use this integration to keep all your services in sync with the same CriptEnv variables.
render.apiKeyWarning: A Render API key has broad access to your account. We recommend creating a key dedicated to the CriptEnv integration.

githubAction.description: Use CriptEnv's official Action (@criptenv/action) to decrypt and inject your environment variables straight into your GitHub Actions workflows.
githubAction.tokenCallout: The CriptEnv GitHub Action needs a valid API token. You can create one in <link>Dashboard → Tokens</link>.

step1.title: Store the CI token and vault password in GitHub
step1.body: In the CriptEnv dashboard, create a CI token (starts with ci_) with the read:secrets scope. Because CriptEnv is zero-knowledge, the token alone only downloads encrypted values: to get plaintext values the Action also needs the project's vault password. Store both as Repository Secrets.

step2.title: Get the project ID
step2.body: Copy your project ID from the CriptEnv dashboard. The action needs it to know which project to decrypt.

step3.title: Add the Action to your workflow
step3.body: Configure your GitHub Actions workflow to run the CriptEnv action before your build or deploy commands.

inputs.title: Inputs
inputs.body: The Action accepts the following inputs:
inputs.token: CriptEnv CI token (starts with ci_). Pass it through GitHub Secrets.
inputs.vaultPassword: Project vault password (via GitHub Secrets). With it, the Action exports plaintext values; without it, variables receive the ciphertext.
inputs.environment: Target environment (e.g. production, staging). Default: production.
inputs.prefix: Prefix for the environment variables. Default: SECRET_.

githubAction.tokenWarning: Never expose the CriptEnv token in public logs. Always use GitHub Secrets to store tokens and sensitive credentials.

teamSetup.description: Learn how to invite members, set permissions and organize your team in CriptEnv to collaborate on secret management securely.

step3.title: Accept the invitation
step3.body: The member gets an email with a link to accept the invitation. Once accepted, they can access the projects according to the permissions you set.

roles.title: Roles and permissions
roles.body: CriptEnv offers 4 permission levels for team members:

perProject.title: Per-project permissions
perProject.body: Permissions are granular per project. A member can be Admin in one project and Viewer in another.

teamSetup.leastPrivilege: Follow the principle of least privilege: grant each member only the permissions they need for their work.
teamSetup.ownerWarning: Members with the Owner role have full access to the project, including deleting it. Limit this role to people you fully trust.

practices.title: CI/CD best practices
practices.environments: Use separate environments: keep different secrets for staging and production
practices.scope: Minimal-scope tokens: create CI/CD-specific tokens with read-only permission

cicd.commitWarning: Never commit CriptEnv tokens to your code. Always use environment variables or the CI/CD platform's native secrets.

migration.title: Migrating .env files
migration.description: Move the variables from an existing .env into the CriptEnv vault and inject them in memory, with no file holding values on disk.

step1.title: Create the project and environment
step1.body: Creating the project sets the vault password: keep it in a password manager. Commands accept the project ID or name.

step2.title: Import the file
step2.body: Each KEY=value line becomes a secret encrypted on the client. Existing keys are kept unless you pass --overwrite.

step3.title: Check nothing was left behind
step3.body: diff compares the file with the vault and exits with code 1 if they differ (also handy as a CI gate).

step4.title: Run the app with secrets in memory
step4.body: run decrypts the values and replaces its own process with the command (signals such as SIGTERM reach the app directly). CriptEnv credentials are not passed to the app.

step5.title: Delete the old file
step5.body: Once everything runs through CriptEnv, delete the file with values and keep only a .env.example with the names.

servers.title: On servers and containers
servers.body: Without a terminal, the CLI reads credentials from the environment: CRIPTENV_API_KEY (a cek_... API key with the read:secrets scope) authenticates the process without writing a session to disk, and CRIPTENV_VAULT_PASSWORD opens the vault. If either is missing, the command fails with an error instead of waiting for a prompt.

migration.exportWarning: criptenv export produces plaintext. If you need it, prefer --format json read directly by the process; in the env format, values with spaces, #, quotes or line breaks are quoted.
